name: Brian Mast
page_title: Brian Mast's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Republican for U.S. House (FL) - District 21

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "The decision to overturn Roe v. Wade will protect millions of innocent babies. Right now, I’m at the Supreme Court for this huge victory for the sanctity of life!"

"That’s why during my time in Congress I have supported legislation to protect the unborn, prohibit taxpayer funding for abortion and increase protections for infants born alive after a failed abortion procedure. I will keep fighting to protect all lives!"
Rated 0% by the Planned Parenthood Action Fund
Rated 100% by the National Right to Life Committee

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: Rated 25% by the National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSM
Voted against S 610 "Protecting Medicare and American Farmers from Sequester Cuts Act"

"I will always protect Social Security and Medicare, ensuring our government keeps the promises it has made to current retirees and those planning to retire. I absolutely do not support cutting benefits for current retirees or anybody nearing retirement. In order to accomplish difficult objectives in times of crisis, I know that we must work together. So, I will continue to be a leading voice for addressing the critical solvency issue of Social Security and Medicare in a bipartisan way that protects care for seniors. In order to accomplish these goals, I’ve helped pass legislation to strengthen Medicare and voted to protect social security beneficiaries."

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: Voted in favor of HR 1 "Tax Cuts and Jobs Act"

"Every dollar spent by the federal government belongs to the American people, and I will keep fighting to return these dollars to where they came from. That’s why I fought hard to successfully pass the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which included cutting taxes, increasing the standard deduction and doubling the child tax credit. I also helped eliminate Obamacare’s costly individual mandate tax. These tax cuts stimulated the economy and led to more investment. Now, we must continue working to close special interest loopholes and lobbyist-driven deductions while making the individual tax cuts permanent!"
"To that end, our current spending is unsustainable, which is why I’ve voted against irresponsible spending packages and why I believe we must pass a Balanced Budget Amendment."

"We must fight for working families by expanding opportunities and creating an economic environment that allows for job growth! First and foremost, that means cutting taxes so every American can keep more of the money they worked hard to earn. Far too often politicians in D.C. forget that the dollars they spend are not theirs. Every dollar spent by the federal government belongs to the American people, and I will keep fighting to return these dollars to where they came from. That’s why I fought hard to successfully pass the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which included cutting taxes, increasing the standard deduction and doubling the child tax credit. "

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "The U.S. just broke another record: the national debt is over $100,000 per citizen. That means my son’s share is more than $100,000. He hasn’t even started kindergarten yet. Washington has to get the spending under control."

"The omnibus is 4,155 pages long. That’s like reading War & Peace 3 times. Those 4,155 pages spend $1.7 trillion of your tax dollars. But rather than allowing us to actually read the bill & debate it, it’s being rammed through at the 11th hour. This isn’t how Congress should work."

"We cannot spend our way out of our debt crisis. Every dollar spent by Washington is a dollar that was earned by We The People. That’s why @HouseGOP is committed to passing individual spending bills that will rein in the out of control deficits."
Voted against HR 3684 "Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "If Democrats in Congress hadn’t pushed through a $1.9 trillion wishlist in 2021, inflation would not be at the levels it is now and our dollars would go further at the grocery store."

"Spending trillions of dollars to ease inflation is like pulling a fire alarm in hopes it will open a door. Neither work. We must cut spending and hold accountable the politicians who put us in this financial mess."
Voted against HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"
"The Inflation "Reduction" Act will increase taxes on working Americans at every income level. Not only does it fail to reduce inflation, but it takes MORE money out of your wallet."

positions.question: Do you support economic intervention as a means of resolving international conflicts?

evidence.text: "I’m introducing legislation to restore President Donald Trump’s sanctions on the International Criminal Court. Trump understood that no globalist organization can bully America or our allies. Joe Biden does not."

"Recent attacks on Israel by Hamas prove once again why we must do more to combat radical Islamic terrorism. Those who support Hamas should be held accountable. That is why I sent a letter urging Speaker Pelosi to expedited consideration of my Hamas sanctions bill."

"While Iran funneled hundreds of millions of dollars to Hamas, Hezbollah and Houthis every year, President Biden gave Tehran an access to over $16 BILLION by waiving sanctions. We need a commander-in-chief who would stop any dollar going to our adversaries."
"HAPPENING NOW: The House is debating my bill to sanction any person, group, or government who backs Hamas and its despicable acts of terrorism. This should be a bipartisan, no-brainer "YES" vote."
